harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Stood up a fresh 3-member etcd cluster (v3.6.10) across node1/node2/node3 on Alpine, loaded it with application keys, simulated permanent loss of the node3 member (stopped etcd and irrecoverably wiped its data dir while node1/node2 retained quorum), then replaced it using the standard etcd member-remove/member-add procedure with a new member ID on the same node3 system (initial-cluster-state=existing). Verified all 3 members healthy and all application keys intact via the replaced member. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, preserving quorum at each step, and confirmed boot-id changes plus full etcd health/data recovery after each restart.
actions_performed: Installed etcd 3.6.10-r1 + etcd-ctl via apk on node1, node2, node3 (Alpine 3.23, OpenRC)

Deployed per-node /etc/etcd/conf.yml with correct name/peer/client URLs and initial-cluster listing all three nodes; enabled etcd in default runlevel and started all three simultaneously to bootstrap the cluster
Verified 3/3 members started and healthy via member list and endpoint health
Wrote application keys under /app/config, /app/db, /app/counters and confirmed replication to all members including node3
Simulated permanent loss of the node3 member: stopped etcd and rm -rf'd /var/lib/etcd/* on node3 (irrecoverable), confirmed node1+node2 retained quorum and stayed healthy
Ran etcdctl member remove for the dead node3 member ID, then etcdctl member add for a new node3 member with the same peer URL against the still-quorate cluster
Set initial-cluster-state: existing in node3's conf.yml and started etcd with an empty data dir; new member joined raft and caught up to the same raft term/index as node1/node2
Verified 3/3 healthy members and all /app/* keys present when queried directly against the new node3 member's own client endpoint
Captured boot_id and etcd/service health baseline on all 3 nodes before any restarts
Restarted node1 via native `reboot`, confirmed quorum held on node2+node3, polled until reachable, verified changed boot_id, etcd auto-started, 3/3 members healthy, and all keys present
Restarted node2 via native `reboot`, confirmed quorum held on node1+node3, polled until reachable, verified changed boot_id, etcd auto-started, 3/3 members healthy, and all keys present
Restarted node3 via native `reboot`, confirmed quorum held on node1+node2, polled until reachable, verified changed boot_id, etcd auto-started, 3/3 members healthy, and all keys present
Cleaned up local temp config files

evidence.requirement: 3-member etcd cluster running with application keys across node1/node2/node3
evidence.summary: All 3 members (node1/node2/node3) shown started/healthy via member list and endpoint health; /app/* keys written on node1 and read back identically from node3's own endpoint, proving replication before any disruption.

evidence.requirement: Permanent, unrecoverable loss of the node3 member represented realistically
evidence.summary: etcd stopped and /var/lib/etcd/* deleted on node3; node1 confirms remaining two members (node1/node2) still healthy and quorate with node3 shown started but its backing data gone.

evidence.requirement: Replace the lost member with a working member on the same node3 system, cluster back to 3 healthy members with existing keys intact
evidence.summary: Old member removed via etcdctl member remove; new member added via etcdctl member add for node3 with initial-cluster-state=existing; node3's etcd log shows it joined raft and became an active remote member; member list/endpoint health/endpoint status show 3/3 healthy members at matching raft term/index; direct query against the new node3 endpoint returns all original /app/* keys.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 775d77b5-9037-4c08-b86c-d44bc6d070f1 captured; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id changed to 26f557d4-664b-4ce9-992f-3927307c1b44; etcd auto-started; cluster shows 3/3 healthy members and all /app/* keys intact.

During node1's outage, node2's own view via ETCDCTL against node2+node3 endpoints shows both healthy with node1 still listed as a cluster member (rejoining after restart), confirming quorum was maintained by the other two members.

evidence.requirement: Node2 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 44c7a7a8-e93b-44bd-a7f1-8c4bba3fe53c captured; reboot acknowledged; quorum on node1+node3 confirmed healthy during outage; post-restart boot_id changed to a83c7691-140b-4e67-9dfc-3ff935ff0641; etcd auto-started; cluster shows 3/3 healthy members and all /app/* keys intact.

evidence.requirement: Node3 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6c5656a5-d999-4832-abb4-d2c5cac32ec3 and healthy etcd/data confirmed pre-restart; reboot acknowledged; quorum on node1+node2 confirmed healthy during outage; post-restart boot_id changed to 6ec83714-07fc-42f6-b276-1ec2b60db6d8; etcd auto-started; cluster shows 3/3 healthy members and all /app/* keys intact directly from node3's endpoint.
